power_purchase.kserc_reasoning: As mentioned in previous paragraphs, as per the Tariff Regulations 2021, if the actual distribution loss is higher than the approved level of distribution loss, then the quantum of power purchased corresponding to the excess distribution loss shall be disallowed at the average cost of power purchase. Accordingly, the power purchase cost based on the approved distribution loss of 3.45% for the year 2022-23 is as shown below.
key_observations: Actual distribution loss (In lakh units): 29.73
Approved distribution loss (In lakh units): 22.99
Excess distribution loss (lakh units) (1-2): 6.74
Average Power Purchase Cost (Rs. per unit): 6.95
Excess power purchase cost to be disallowed (Rs. lakh) (4) * (3): 46.84

employee_cost.kserc_reasoning: Considering the above, the Commission hereby approves the employee cost of Rs. 27.82 lakh for the year 2022-23 as per the norm after adjusting actual inflation.
key_observations: Actual employee cost claimed by the licensee is Rs. 54.54 lakh as against the approved norms of Rs. 27.14 lakh.
The actual employee is higher compared to the norms.
Major items booked under Employee Cost are Consolidated pay, salaries, dearness allowances, HRA, other allowance etc.
employee_cost.methodology_applied: As per the norm after adjusting actual inflation (Annexure-7 of Tariff Regulations, 2021, and actual inflation rate of 7.06%)

repair_maintenance.kserc_reasoning: The commission noted that as per the provision 80 (3) of the regulations, 'Any one time operation and maintenance expenditure of a special nature not in the form of routine repair and maintenance, if any, if required and is undertaken by the distribution licensee, expenses for such maintenance may be allowed by the commission after prudence check, considering the circumstances, details and justification furnished by the Distribution business/licensee for incurring such an expenditure, to the satisfaction of the commission'. This provision allows onetime expenses incurred, not in the nature of regular R&M expenses. Considering this, the Commission hereby approves the one-time repair and maintenance charges of Rs. 35.60 lakh together with the cost of material and spares amounting to Rs.11.16 lakh purchase for the same in addition to the norms as claimed by the licensee. The Commission also notes that the new campus at Pallippuram Technocity was commissioned in 2019-20 whereas the norms for O&M expenses were fixed based on trued up figures of 2018-19. As such, the O&M expenses for the Pallippuram Technocity are not reflected in the norm. The licensee submitted that Rs.30.38 lakh has been spent towards R&M expenses of Pallippuram Technocity. The Commission considers this and is of the opinion to allow these expenses over and above the norm. Therefore the Commission approves Rs.30.38 lakh as R&M expenses for Technocity in addition to the norms. The Commission examined the arguments of the licensee regarding the normative amount approved in the regulations, 2021. The commission had considered the revised R&M based on actual escalation rate for the year 2022-23. Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves Rs. 402.43 lakh (Rs. 35.60 lakh + Rs. 11.16 lakh + Rs.30.38 lakh + Rs. 325.29 lakh) as R&M expense for the year 2022-23.
key_observations: Claimed Rs. 447.65 lakh against normative Rs. 317.37 lakh.
Licensee states R&M carried out by licensed electrical contractors through transparent competitive bidding.
Overall increase of 10.57% compared to previous year, including new distribution area under Phase-IV in Pallippuram (Rs. 30.38 lakh).
One-time repair and maintenance charges of Rs. 35.60 lakh approved.
Cost of material and spares of Rs. 11.16 lakh approved.
R&M expenses for Technocity of Rs. 30.38 lakh approved over and above the norm.
repair_maintenance.methodology_applied: Provision 80 (3) of the regulations for one-time expenses; revised R&M based on actual escalation rate for the year 2022-23.

admin_general.kserc_reasoning: The Commission examined the submission of the licensee and observed that, the licensee has booked Rs. 36.98 lakh towards Electricity Duty for the year 2022-23. The Commission in the previous Orders had stated that duty under Section 3 cannot be passed on to the consumers in view of the statutory provisions of the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963. Hence the same is disallowed. Considering the methodology in approving the operation and maintenance expenses based on the actual escalation for the year, the commission hereby approves the amount of Rs. 36.99 lakh as A&G expenses for the year 2022-23
key_observations: Claimed Rs. 92.05 lakh against approved norm Rs. 36.09 lakh.
Includes Rs. 36.98 lakh towards Electricity Duty, which is disallowed.
Major expenses include Electricity charges (Rs. 12.10 lakh), Fees to Electrical Inspectorate (Rs. 14.80 lakh), conveyance charges (Rs. 5.52 lakh).
40% of electricity charges for administrative offices apportioned to distribution business.
admin_general.methodology_applied: Disallowance of Electricity Duty under Section 3 of Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963; approval based on actual escalation for the year.

depreciation.kserc_reasoning: Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves depreciation of Rs.94.17 lakh for the year 2019-20, Rs. 96.59 for the year 2020-21, Rs. 75.50 lakh for the year 2021-22 and Rs. 75.43 lakh for the year 2022-23 as per the revised calculation as shown above. Accordingly, the Commission hereby claws back Rs. 162.56 lakh as excess amount of depreciation provisionally approved in previous years.
key_observations: Licensee claimed Rs. 162.45 lakh.
No depreciation claimed for assets from Government grants and consumer contributions.
No asset capitalization during the year 2022-23.
Assets worth Rs. 1.73 lakh withdrawn from assets.
depreciation.methodology_applied: Revised calculation based on detailed asset information and disallowance for assets created by utilizing regulatory surplus.

interest_long_term.kserc_reasoning: As per the above table the Commission hereby approves Rs. 8.50 lakh as interest on normative loan for the year 2022-23 and allows an extra amount of Rs. 15.61 lakh as adjustments against interest on normative loan allowed in the past years. Comparison of approved and revised calculation of interest on normative loan is given below:
key_observations: Licensee claimed Rs. 8.96 lakh interest on normative loan.
Weighted average interest rate for 2022-23 is 8.49%.
interest_long_term.methodology_applied: Revised calculation of normative loan and interest charges, including adjustments for past years.

interest_consumer_deposits.kserc_reasoning: The interest on security deposits paid to the consumers for the year 2022-23 as claimed by the licensee amounts to Rs.72.70 lakh as against the ARR&ERC approved amount of Rs. 63.91 lakh. The Commission hereby approves the actual amount of Rs. 72.70 lakh paid by the licensee as interest on security deposits for the year 2022-23.
key_observations: ARR&ERC approved amount was Rs. 63.91 lakh.
interest_consumer_deposits.methodology_applied: Approved as claimed based on actual amount paid.

return_on_nfa.kserc_reasoning: As per the above table the Commission hereby approves Rs. 35.95 lakh as RoNFA for the year 2022-23 and claws back Rs. 14.23 lakh as excess amount of RoNFA allowed in the past years. Comparison of approved and revised calculation of RoNFA is given below:
key_observations: Licensee claimed Rs. 86.60 lakh at 5.50% on NFA of Rs. 1574.46 lakh.
Assets created by utilizing regulatory surplus are not eligible for RoNFA.
return_on_nfa.methodology_applied: Revised calculation based on decisions on capital investments and depreciation, and clawback of excess RoNFA from previous years.

other_debits.kserc_reasoning: The petitioner states that the working capital requirement has increased to Rs. 1007.87 lakh due to higher sales, compared to Rs. 765.44 lakh and Rs. 752.75 lakh in the previous two years. The consumer deposit in cash is Rs. 1790.88 lakh, which was sufficient to cover the working capital requirement. Therefore, there were no additional borrowings required for working capital. Hence no interest on working capital is claimed by the licensee.
key_observations: Licensee did not claim interest on working capital.

energy_decision.kserc_reasoning: Accordingly, as per the provisions of the Tariff Regulations, distribution loss is a controllable performance parameter. As per regulation 73(3) of the Tariff Regulations, 2021, if actual distribution loss is higher than the approved level, the quantum of power purchased corresponding to the excess distribution loss shall be disallowed at the average power purchase cost. The Commission hereby decides to limit the distribution loss to the approved level of 3.45% for the purpose of truing up. The licensee is directed to take effective measures to limit the distribution loss at the approved level.
energy_decision.excess_demand_action: The quantum of power purchased corresponding to the excess distribution loss for that financial year shall be disallowed at the average power purchase cost.

capital_structure_verified.kserc_reasoning: Considering the submissions made by the licensee, the Commission approves the capital investments made by the licensee. The Commission allows to meet the own fund requirements (excluding grant received from government) of Rs. 322.11 lakh (Rs.323.84 lakh - Rs.1.73 lakh) from the approved regulatory surplus of Rs.2267.07 lakh as on 31-03-2020 vide truing up order for the year 2019-20 dated 16-02-2022 (OP No.48/2021). The Commission has been allowing all reasonable and prudent expenses including RoE/ Return on net fixed assets to Technopark over the years for carrying out its electricity distribution activities. The accrued regulatory surplus approved and allowed to be retained with the Licensee is the amount arrived at after allowing all the prudent expenses including statutory returns. Accordingly, the licensee shall not be eligible for depreciation, RoE/RoNFA and other financing costs on the assets created by utilising such surplus as it would result in double payment by the consumers.
